The front door stands open on the dripping gravel; the carriage glass is fogged, and behind it two hands are folded over the place a watch used to hang.

Fairbrother takes the house keys at the stair foot without looking up, the ring closing in his old hand as if it had always been there. The front door stands open on the dripping gravel; behind the carriage glass the Major is leaning across to Mr Ellingham, talking, and does not stop.

The front door is open and the carriage waits on the gravel. The Major sits very upright behind the glass, hands folded over his empty watch pocket, saying nothing at all. Fairbrother stands with the house keys in his hand and Dr Ashcombe by the coat stand, pulling on his gloves slowly.

The front door is open and the carriage waits on the gravel. Behind the glass the Major is talking the length of a sentence into Mr Ellingham's ear, and the word that carries across the step is 'housekeeper'. Fairbrother holds the house keys and Dr Ashcombe stands by the coat stand, finding something to do with his gloves.

The front door stands open on grey light and the sound of water running off the porch. The carriage waits on the gravel with its two passengers; the house keys have changed hands at the stair foot; Dr Ashcombe is by the coat stand with his bag, in no hurry to go out to it.

housekeeper_s_room.text: Your box is roped and stood on end by the stove. Lavinia has her shawl on to carry it and keeps one hand closed in her apron pocket. The key board has your ring still on its hook, the only thing in the room that is not yet packed or paid.

Your box is roped by the stove and Lavinia stands over it with her arms folded, waiting to be told to lift it. The character and the coin lie on the deal desk. The old housekeeper's bonnet hangs where it always hung; yours will not join it.
The stove is nearly out and no one will make it up again for you. Your box is roped, your wages are on the desk, and your ring of keys hangs on the key board under the dead woman's bonnet.

drawing_room.text: Miss Gresham sits at the sofa table with her ring on her finger and a sheet of paper under her hand, which she turns face down when the door opens. Mrs Ormsby on the window seat watches the carriage through the glass and does not turn round.

Miss Gresham is at the sofa table, saying to no one and everyone that the housekeeper went through pockets; she does not say whose. Mrs Ormsby on the window seat has her own letter already sealed and addressed to town.

The fire has been let burn low; nobody has rung for coal. Miss Gresham sits at the sofa table and Mrs Ormsby on the window seat, both of them with the composure of women who have been left in possession of a house.

interactions.text: You take the ring from your waist and hang it on its hook under the old housekeeper's bonnet. Thirty-one keys, every one of which you could name in the dark. The study key is not among them and never will be now.

Fairbrother weighs the house keys in his palm. Either he says, loud enough for the groom in the yard, that a woman who saw a tallow stub at ten paces was wasted below stairs, and goes down himself for your box; or he says 'Yes, Mrs—' and cannot finish the name, and turns to the stair, and your box goes down with the maid.
interactions.detail_label: 'He is yours to keep now, Mr Fairbrother.'

interactions.text: You go out by the front door, which is not the door you came in by. The carriage has turned on the gravel and gone down through the thaw with the key and the stub and two gentlemen who will not speak of a will. The cart waits at the side with your box in it; the groom has something in his glove that may be a letter, unsigned, in a lady's hand, or may be nothing. The house drips behind you and does not watch you go.

events.text: The carriage wheels bite the gravel and it turns and goes down the drive through the melting snow. Behind the glass, as it passes the window, the Major's hands are either folded and still over his empty watch pocket, or moving as he talks.

nudges.text: From the yard, the groom's voice carries through the house: the road will not keep soft all day, and he means to be at the lodge before it freezes again.
Somewhere above, Fairbrother tries the house keys one by one in the baize door, the way the dead woman used to, learning them.

text.text: Lucius Carrington is driven down the thawing road to the magistrate on the housekeeper's word, the valet's confession and the doctor's certificate; the nephew is cleared, but his marriage, the doctor's practice and the widow's name were broken in the same quarter hour, the valet leaves by the first cart with no character after forty years, and the master is remembered as a man who sold his silence for thirty years before he thought to buy it back.

variants.text: Goes down the drive with his coat buttoned over the decoration and does not once look at the servant who put him there; he had never thought her worth watching, and still does not.
Says your name to the magistrate before his own, a housekeeper who kept a dead man's candle-end in her apron, and the solicitor spends the whole road unsaying it.

variants.text: Carries forty years down the back stairs in one box; at the foot he sets your candle box square on its shelf before he goes, and that is all the leave he takes of you.
Goes without a character and without a word. The kitchen has it from him that the new housekeeper counted candles over a dying man's order.

variants.text: Returns the ring and leaves with her chin up, the sherry understood by the room as begging and not as murder; she will not look at the woman who said it aloud, though she knows it was the kinder word.
Returns the ring without a word to Nathaniel of why she went to the study, and lets the house think what it likes of a glass that was held over her for two days.
variants.note: fallback: the last variant holds otherwise

variants.text: Leaves on the doctor's arm with the hairpin gone down the road in a labelled paper; her thanks for your discretion about the midnight stairs is a silence, and she keeps it.
Mentions to the magistrate's man, in passing, that the housekeeper kept ladies' hairpins in her apron, and lets him draw his own conclusions.

variants.text: Given notice, she passes you on the stairs without a word, her apron clean; but she will not say to the kitchen that it was you who sent her up.
Given notice before the kitchen, ash still on her apron. She tells the carter the housekeeper made her do it, and the carter tells the village.

text.text: Millicent Gresham is driven down the thawing road in the Major's carriage on the housekeeper's word and the lipstick glass, with Carrington beside her to deliver the household's account; Nathaniel is unlocked and cleared and goes to the stables without looking at you. Fairbrother thanks you at the sideboard for never having asked him the hour, Lavinia brings your tea as she always has, the widow keeps her letter and the ward her lie, and the master's oldest friend sits in the master's chair at dinner. You lock the study at night with the key he hands you across the table, and the story ends there, in the one way it can be lost: an innocent at the magistrate's and the killer at the fire.

variants.text: Carves in the master's chair, hands you the study key across the table, and speaks your surname to the room as a man speaks of a sergeant he can rely on.
Still at the head of the table, still the house's guest of honour; the study key stays on his own chain, and your notice is written before Twelfth Night.

variants.text: Thanks you for never asking him the hour, and from that evening the linen comes up folded the way you asked for it.
Serves the Major's table with the hour still in his keeping and watches you from the sideboard, a man who knows exactly what you let go down the road.

variants.text: In the hall, cloak on, she stops and says quite clearly that she had asked you as a woman; then she gets into the carriage.
Goes out to the carriage without a cloak until the Major sends for one; her eyes pass over you as over a sideboard.

variants.text: Her letter lies in the desk unfound and the doctor's door is never mentioned; she praises your discretion to the Major at dinner, and this time means it.
Stays on as the Major's guest, as languid as ever on the stairs; she has her own maid dress her now, and does not ring for you.

variants.text: Brings your tea without being rung for and whispers that the grate is relit and nobody has asked about her candle.
Brings your tea because she is told to, sets it down and goes; the kitchen hears nightly how you left her to the study alone.

text.text: Lucius Carrington is held by the arms on the gallery where the door came down, named by the master's key set in the lock from the gallery side and the lamp you saw through the empty keyhole before the poker was fetched, with the study as it was found behind him and not one servant's word in the case; the carriage takes him down the dripping road with the solicitor beside him, and the unsigned will in the desk is never spoken of. Fairbrother keeps his forty years and his silence, Lavinia her place, Millicent her ring and her ten o'clock, the widow her letter, the doctor his practice; and Nathaniel Yardley, master under the old will, gives the housekeeper who put her hand in a gentleman's pocket her wages, her character, and the next cart.

variants.text: Sits in the carriage with his hands folded over the place his watch hung and says nothing the whole way down.
The mark of his hand still on your cheek when the carriage turns; he tells Ellingham the length of the drive that the housekeeper was in the heir's pay.

variants.text: Takes the house keys from the heir and sees your box to the cart himself; in the yard he tells the groom a woman who saw a tallow stub at ten paces was wasted below stairs.
Takes the keys at the foot of the stairs without lifting his head. Your box goes down with the maid, not with him.

variants.text: Her hour never spoken, the ring still on her hand; she sends a character after you by the groom, unsigned, in a lady's writing.
Still engaged, still mistress-to-be. She speaks at tea of a housekeeper who went through pockets, and does not mean the Major's.

variants.text: Knelt at the keyhole with the lawyer and saw nothing; she sends word by Ashcombe that if you want a place in town, she knows a house that is not particular about characters.
Still in the house, still courteous, still circling. She had written to town that morning about a housekeeper who frightened the guests.

variants.text: Hauls your box to the cart muttering she never thought you had it in you, and at the step slips a tallow stub into your hand: the one from her own room.
Hauls your box to the cart because the valet told her to, and does not stay to see it off.
